why: The OpenAI manuscript appears twice (openai-2026-serre-positivity-preprint, second-hand; openai-math-193, read from the tex); both rows answer it identically: Theorem 1.1 is the module form for every regular local ring, which contains the statement's quotient form, so scope is whole; it is unreviewed, and doubtful rather than not_credible because the concerns are compressed steps and an internal inconsistency, not an identified fatal error. AI role is generated: the paper's author line is 'OpenAI' and the README says the manuscripts were produced by the internal model; the quote is collection-wide, which is the close call. Bhatt-Hochster-Ma scored none: its mixed-characteristic result is conditional on unproven lim CM sequences, and its equal-characteristic positivity re-proves a case already settled by Serre, so it settles nothing new. Kc-Soto Levins is a case (Serre liftable modules, including some ramified rings), journal-accepted. Vanishing and nonnegativity results are variants (different parts of Serre's conjecture). The Hochster note has a year-only 2024 date, so after_snapshot is null.
doubts: The two OpenAI rows are one event split in two by the record. The AI attribution rests on a repository-wide README sentence, not a paper-specific statement. BHM's journal acceptance and Kc-Soto Levins's IMRN publication come from search summaries, not opened pages. Whether BHM's equal-characteristic statement goes beyond Serre's 1965 results is unresolved in the record; if it does, it would be a case rather than none, without changing the outcome's tier ordering.
